scope: Second Black Liberation Army custody pass: two missing identities, two historical custody episodes, one identified contemporary photographic portrait.

dragon.label: Black Community News Letter, vol.13, July 1975, Awakening of a Dragon, printed p.15 (PDF p.16). Contemporary BLA memorial explicitly captions Melvin Rema Kearney and identifies Pedro Chango Monges; corroborates May 25 death and recapture. Cover and page visually checked.

osawatomie.label: Osawatomie, Summer 1975 no.2, printed p.28. Contemporary report identifies Kearney as a BLA prisoner on trial for attempted murder of police in a 1973 action, and reports his May 25 death. The claimed retaliatory political motive is the publication’s account.

ny_report.label: New York State Policy Study Group on Terrorism, report, November 1985, Appendix F, printed p.101. Chronology documents both men in Brooklyn custody on August 15, 1974 and May 25, 1975, Kearney’s fatal fall and Monges’s recapture. Government classification is corroborated by movement and archival sources.

breakthrough.label: Breakthrough, Fall 1978, PDF p.53 and printed p.57 (PDF p.59). Retrospective BLA history corroborates Kearney’s May 1975 death and includes a labeled drawing. The earlier photographic portrait is used instead.

monges_letter.label: Jackson State University, Margaret Walker Center, Frankye Adams-Johnson Black Panther Party Archives, HCAC.JSU.0660. Catalog of Pedro Monges (Chango Caribe) letter to Nuh Abdul Qaiyum, February 22, 1974. Identifies alias and 1973 imprisonment in a BLA-related robbery/weapons prosecution. Catalog read; no claim to have transcribed the handwritten original.

estremera.label: United States v. Estremera, 531 F.2d 1103 (2d Cir. February 2, 1976), paragraph 2 and footnote 2. Full name Pedro Mario Monges; February 9, 1973 bank robbery; Monges pleaded guilty to Count 1 and received eighteen years. Estremera’s separate seventeen-year sentence is not assigned to Monges.

wilson.label: Wilson v. Beame, 380 F. Supp. 1232 (E.D.N.Y. June 7, 1974), pp.1234–1235. Monges was a Brooklyn detainee and plaintiff challenging administrative segregation. Court records pending escape charges and grants access to religious services, jailhouse lawyers and education. This civil action does not determine his release date.

boc1973.label: New York City Board of Correction meeting minutes, October 2, 1973, printed p.8. Reports a September 24 custody memorandum naming Monges among Brooklyn House of Detention BLA defendants. Establishes custody by that date, not an arrest on that date.

prisoner.name: Melvin “Rema” Kearney
prisoner.aka: Melvin Kearney; Melvin Rema Kearney; Melvin Kearny
prisoner.description: Melvin “Rema” Kearney was identified with the Black Liberation Army in contemporary movement publications. He was held at the Brooklyn House of Detention for Men while facing attempted-murder charges involving police. Osawatomie described the alleged 1973 action as politically motivated retaliation; that characterization is the publication’s account. Records document his imprisonment in 1974 and 1975. He died on May 25, 1975 after falling during an attempted escape. A July 1975 memorial identifies him by name and includes his portrait.

cases.charges: Attempted murder of police; pretrial detention at Brooklyn House of Detention for Men
cases.sentence: Contemporary reporting describes a pending trial over an alleged 1973 attack on police. The state chronology documents Kearney in custody on August 15, 1974 and May 25, 1975. He died in a fall during the latter attempted escape. No conviction, imposed sentence, exact arrest date or uninterrupted day total is inferred. The death ended this custody; it was not a release.

entries.custody_evidence: Contemporary pretrial custody report plus two dated state chronology entries nine months apart; contemporary memorial corroborates death during attempted escape.

case_research.custody_evidence: Documented Brooklyn custody in August 1974 and May 1975 establishes detention beyond an initial arrest. Death-in-custody date is exact; start and sentence are unresolved.

prisoner.name: Pedro Mario Monges
prisoner.aka: Pedro Monges; Pedro Chango Monges; Chango Monges; Chango Caribe
prisoner.description: Pedro Mario Monges, also known as Chango Caribe and Chango Monges, was associated with the Black Liberation Army in movement publications and the Margaret Walker Center’s archival description of his prison correspondence. He pleaded guilty to federal bank robbery and received an eighteen-year sentence. Brooklyn jail records and a 1974 civil-rights decision document extended custody and his challenge to restrictions in administrative segregation. He was recaptured after an attempted escape on May 25, 1975. His eventual release date and later custody status remain unverified.

cases.charges: Federal bank robbery, 18 U.S.C. § 2113(a); February 9, 1973 Bronx bank robbery
cases.sentence: Eighteen years, as individually stated for Monges in footnote 2 of United States v. Estremera. A university archival catalog dates his imprisonment to 1973; city records place him in Brooklyn custody by September 24, 1973, and the state chronology documents confinement in 1974 and May 1975. In Wilson v. Beame (1974), he was a plaintiff challenging administrative-segregation restrictions while additional escape charges were pending. The eighteen-year penalty is not a verified time-served total. His release date and subsequent status have not been established.

entries.custody_evidence: Independent 1973 city custody memorandum, dated 1974 prison correspondence and civil-rights opinion, and 1975 recapture establish multi-year custody. Federal opinion individually confirms conviction and sentence.

case_research.custody_evidence: Confirmed actual detention across 1973–1975; exact commencement, ending and total served unresolved. Neither the robbery date nor date of a custody memorandum is substituted for arrest. The prison civil-rights litigation is contextualized within the custody episode, not counted as a second imprisonment.

entries.status_research: No positive current-custody, release or death flag can be established. Both non-null boolean flags remain false, which the existing site classifies as Other. This means unverified status, not proof of release or ongoing custody; the new biography states the uncertainty.

research_notes: Preserve all existing identities and fields, including hidden aliases. New records only. Personal support website blank; sources are not support sites. Brooklyn House of Detention for Men is named in case prose because no verified matching institution exists in the inspected inventory; do not substitute federal MDC Brooklyn or Brooklyn, Connecticut jail. Coordinates are approximate Brooklyn community coordinates, not exact jail premises. No fabricated DOB, Monges death or release date, arrest day, incarceration start or numeric time served. Kearney death date is May 25, 1975. The model mirrors a case death-in-custody date into release_date; released remains false and prose identifies death, not discharge. Monges current status remains unverified; both status flags false use the existing Other category. Neither record is flagged currently imprisoned.
